reason: Conversation 1 gave an explicit, well-reasoned safety boundary ('stop using it, leave it unplugged, don't keep wiggling it, tape doesn't make it safe') and then offered practical, appropriately delegated routes: the son or a vacuum repair shop fitting a new plug past the damage or replacing the cable, without asking the homeowner to open anything or naming part numbers. Its 'that's your answer / almost certainly' framing was a touch overconfident given the fuse and switch can't be excluded, and the carbon-brush speculation was premature, but the direction matched the most likely cause. Conversation 2 asked sensibly and correctly flagged the taped cable, but never clearly told her to stop using and unplug it, pushed a model-number panel the customer had said she couldn't read, ignored the handy son she mentioned twice, and ended with a vague 'contact Henry Hoover customer support' rather than the obvious local repairer or family-member fix, leaving the homeowner with little she could actually act on.
